title: Seen
brief: Invent one new widget that goes beyond everything in the catalog. One remarkable idea, or none.

stamps.reason: The engine's guess is not hidden: it is already shown dim in the prompt box for Tab to take, so there is nothing sealed to turn over and what is left is a tally in the family of wager-widget and nextup-widget.
stamps.subject: Predictable

stamps.reason: The cut-off sentence is not lost, it stays in the transcript where the turn stopped, so the card is a list of text already on screen that changes nothing the person does.
stamps.subject: Interrupted

stamps.reason: It is changes-widget, activity-widget, tasks-widget and pen-widget read together at the moment of an abort, and the transcript already shows which calls finished; only the never-applied edit is new, which is too little for a card.
stamps.subject: Aftermath

stamps.reason: The note cannot arrive in time: the import is seen only after Claude has written the code, and it rests on a hand-kept table of model cutoff dates plus sending package names to a registry, a cost out of proportion to a hint Claude gets from the first build error.
stamps.subject: After Claude's Time

stamps.reason: It predicts only from calls already seen and the types say the classifier is not consulted on a query, so in the modes people actually leave running its answer is wrong or empty, and what is left is guard-widget's list read ahead of time.
stamps.subject: Walkaway

stamps.reason: At rest it reads '12 yours, 0 not' for nearly every session, the cost side is ledger-widget and usage-widget split by one more column, and the hold verb rests on an unconfirmed claim that a /loop or cron firing raises session.receive at all.
stamps.subject: Uninvited

stamps.reason: Not chosen: the strongest runner-up, but it is stakes-widget's dialog line measuring a second thing, it is silent for anyone without kubectl, aws or gcloud, and guessing a command's target from its first word (ignoring --context, --profile and inline env) risks a false all-clear on the one command that matters.
stamps.subject: Aim

stamps.reason: Not chosen: a real one-sentence story and the API holds, but it is a novelty that changes nothing the person does and it puts text they chose to delete back on screen, where Seen closes a gap in trust on every screenshot.
stamps.subject: Unsaid

stamps.reason: Seen is the only idea that adds a sense the catalog lacks: it shows the pictures Claude judged from, which no widget and no part of the terminal does, uses the unused Image element, costs no tokens, and changes what the person does by letting them check the evidence instead of the claim.

No blocking fault: every hook and call is in the 2.1.289 types, all five states are drawn, the box sums hold, the demo and live sections are present and the spec is 108 lines with 15 acceptance lines; 12 notes in spec-notes.md, chiefly the cut rows at 20 columns and the 10 s hook budget for the decode.

State and storage cannot hold what the spec asks: $.state.set refuses any one value over 4,194,304 characters of JSON ('$.state.set: the value is 4195002 characters, over the 4194304 limit', measured in claude plugin test on 2.1.289), and kept is one Record value meant to hold up to four pictures of up to 4,000,000 base64 characters each (16 MB), so as soon as the held pictures pass 4.19M characters together (two ordinary 1.5 MB screenshots) the newest is listed but its bytes are not kept and neither Image nor open can show it. Design must choose: kept as a StateFamily with one picture per id (4,000,000 characters plus the media fits one member), or a smaller per-picture or total budget, or keeping only the newest, and restate Kept, State, Cost, A7, A9 and A11 to match. The rest is built in factory/floor/plugins/seen-widget and passes 19 of 20 tests; only the last step of A9 (a 1.4M-character PNG after a 2.8M-character one) fails, on this limit. For note 4: the pure inflate takes about 0.6 s for 1920x1080 and 1.3 to 2.0 s for 8,000,000 pixels under bun.

No blocking fault: the build send-back is answered by making kept a StateFamily with one picture per slot, which the 2.1.289 types support, and Kept, State, Cost, A7, A9 and A11 now agree; 109 lines, 15 acceptance lines; 15 notes in spec-notes.md, chiefly the unmeasured 16M total of state and the cut rows at 20 columns.

Built seen-widget to the revised spec: kept is a StateFamily with one picture per slot (id % 4), draw and open believe a slot only when its id equals the shot's, and all 15 acceptance tests plus the standard tests pass, including four kept pictures of 4,000,000 characters each (16M of state accepted in claude plugin test on 2.1.289) and the 8,000,000 pixel decode cap kept as written (1.3 to 2.0 s, inside the 10 s hook budget).

The thumb decode cannot meet the spec in the plugin runtime: measured in claude plugin test it costs about 2.1 microseconds a pixel in the tool.call hook (1280x720 2.0-2.5 s, 1920x1080 4.2-5.2 s, 2880x1800 11 s, 8,000,000 pixels 17 s, four 1080p blocks in one MCP call 18 s), about eight times the bun figure the 8,000,000 pixel cap rests on, so pictures under the cap overrun the 10,000 ms hook budget and are dropped with an error, and every ordinary screenshot holds Claude's result back for seconds; design must set a measured ceiling and say where and how the thumb is made and what shows past it. For the next build: check.ts failed 3 of 5 runs because test A4 sits on the default 5 s limit, a Read with no file_path makes the card vanish, and two small answer faults; see inspection.md.

No blocking fault: the inspection send-back is answered by moving the thumb decode out of the tool.call hook into a sliced timer job with a measured 4,200,000 pixel ceiling and a plain no-preview row past it, the slice arithmetic and every named call hold against the 2.1.289 types, and the spec is 117 lines with 15 acceptance lines; 16 notes in spec-notes.md, chiefly where the base64 is decoded and whether the slices keep the session responsive.

Rebuilt seen-widget to the third spec: the tool.call hook only lists the picture (PNG header from the first 44 base64 characters, no pixel decoded) and a sync-started 5 ms timer job draws the newest eligible PNG's thumb in row slices with the base64 decoded block by block inside the generator, plus the (no path) and control-character sources, the usage past 9 digits and the one-separator page path; measured in claude plugin test on 2.1.289 with a realistic 1920x1080 RGBA screenshot (1.19 MB file): capture 1 to 2 ms of the hook's own time (14 to 17 ms in the hook with its state calls, 37 ms for four 1080p blocks in one MCP call), 135 slices, 1.37 s of decode in all, longest slice 23 ms (63 ms for the first cold slice of a 1280x720), and check.ts passed five runs in a row.

Third build meets the spec, the standard and the bar: check.ts passed three runs in a row, the live run shows the real Read result listed and its thumb drawn by the timer with only isOn in the store, a realistic 1920x1080 screenshot is captured in about 50 ms of wall time and drawn in 135 slices over 1.7 s with no tick above 22 ms, and odd inputs and parallel reads neither throw nor lose a picture; six notes in inspection.md, chiefly wide-character paths and the owner's one hand run of open.
On the demo page, in the README and the marketplace; smoke test clean
